stories.title: CM Chandrababu Naidu promises full support to farmers hit by cyclone
stories.summary: Power restoration by Saturday evening in cyclone affected areas
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Friday assured cyclone-hit farmers, fishermen and families that the government would extend assistance to every affected person.
He said the preliminary assessment put Cyclone Arnab losses at Rs 4,600 crore and a comprehensive damage assessment would be submitted to the Centre soon.

During his visit to Kothanavarasapuram in Narsapuram mandal and Matrevu in Mogalthur mandal of West Godavari district, Naidu inspected inundated fields and damaged coconut plantations and interacted with farmers.
He enquired about crop insurance coverage and said the government had taken steps to cover every acre through the e-Crop system.
Input subsidies would help compensate farmers for their losses, he added.
At the cyclone relief centre in Matrevu, women recalled their anxiety during the cyclone, while fishermen from the Vasista Godavari region explained their difficulties.
Naidu directed officials to desilt the canal near the sea mouth to facilitate fishing.
He also inspected electricity restoration works and appreciated personnel clearing fallen trees and repairing infrastructure.
Addressing the media, Naidu said the government had held continuous reviews and teleconferences with field staff to minimise casualties and restore normalcy.
However, seven people had lost their lives.
More than 15,000 electricity poles had collapsed across affected areas, and power supply would be fully restored by Saturday evening.
Household connections would receive priority, followed by agricultural supply.

article_sentences: Road repair work on the trumpet interexchange leading to the Alluri Sitarama Raju international airport was taken up on war footing on Friday evening after sections of the road got damaged and reportedly collapsed at certain places due to the impact of ‘Cyclone Arnab’.
The route is important for air travellers, who had raised concerns over the safety of the road and asked GMR authorities to take up repairs immediately.
Vizianagaram Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy had reportedly alerted the executives of the group to the damage, pointing out that many VIPs travel the route.
He asked them to verify the reasons for the damage of the road, which happened within three months after the inauguration of the airport.
With pressure from government, the contractors took up repair works temporarily and assured to relay the road shortly.

stories.headline: Flood Control in Jhelum: HC seeks report on mining activities, STPs, embankments
stories.title: Flood Control in Jhelum: HC seeks report on mining activities, STPs, embankments
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 30: The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir has sought a report attesting to mining activities, proposed setting up of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) in river Jehlum as also construction or removal of embankments for flood control of the waterbody. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Dr Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Yash Paul Bourney sought the report after Advocate Nadeem Qadiri assisting as amicus curiae in the Public Interest Litigation (PIL) by Environmental Policy Group on conservation of Jehlum, raised these issues. “What is the kind of legal or illegal mining activity is going on in the entire river Jhelum? How many STPs have been proposed to be established in the course of river Jhelum? And how many of the embankments have been built or removed for the purpose of containing the flood?” the amicus said at the very outset. Following the Court counsel’s submission, senior Additional Advocate General for the government informed the court that he would respond to all the issues. Furthermore, he would explain the execution of the affidavit filed by the Divisional Commissioner on October 25, he said The Court however directed the senior AAG to indicate also the milestones achieved so far in the matter related to flood mitigation. It listed the matter for further hearing on October 31. Filed in 2017, the PIL flags the fragile flood management system in Kashmir. It seeks the court's intervention for measures to protect Kashmir from future flood disasters. The PIL also highlights the shortcomings in flood management due to which massive damage was caused during 2014 floods and seeks tangible steps to avoid such situations.

stories.headline: Israel: Heading to another election?
stories.title: Israel: Heading to another election?
stories.summary: The elections to the 120-member Israeli Knesset which were held on October 27 were closely watched in the region. This was primarily because they were expected to indicate the support which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had among the Israeli people for the pursuit of the Iran war. Netanyahu’s Likud party along with its rightwing coalition partners went all out to woo voters to their cause but the result was fractured. It demonstrated the political and social contentions within Israel in general and also on the Iran war. Israeli elections are held on a proportional basis. That means that voters do not vote for particular candidates but for political parties. Generally, each party, even in a coalition, puts up separate lists. The number of seats allotted to a party depends on the number of votes it has got provided it crosses the threshold of 3.25 % of the total vote. The entire country is treated as one constituency. The result of this complex election process is that no single party succeeds in getting a majority on its own strength. Hence, coalitions are formed. The coalition situation prior to the October 27 election was thus: Netanyahu’s Likud led party coalition had 68 seats. It had won 64 seats in the 2022 elections but four members of another party had later joined it to raise its number to 68; the Jewish opposition parties 42 and the two Israeli-Arab parties 10. The results led to a sharp drop in the Netanyahu led Likud party coalitions. It secured only a vote share which would give it 53 seats. Meanwhile the Jewish bloc which is now under the leadership of former head of the Israeli defence forces, Gadi Eisenkot managed to get 48 seats based on its vote share. At the same time there was a dramatic increase in the share of the Israeli Arab parties from 10 to 19. The consequence of this break-up is that no coalition has sufficient number of seats to form a government on its own. It also means that Netanyahu has suffered a definite reverse but it has not been strong enough to oust him. This reverse has led the Israeli Prime Minister to claim that Qatar has sought to manipulate the election. On their part the Qataris have angrily and outrightly denied this charge. Most Israeli officials have rejected the charge of foreign manipulation in the election. However, Justice Noam Scholberg who was head of the Central Election Committee overseeing these elections claimed, according to news reports, that he had been shown some “exceptionally grave” information of foreign funding coming to these elections by Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security agency. Consequently, he has asked for Shin Bet to give its findings within the next few days. Clearly, the target of this charge of foreign funding are the Israeli Arab parties. On their part they have denied them. However, one Likud party spokesman was quoted in the media as saying “The Ra’amgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Ra’am is one of the Arab parties. Meanwhile, while going along with the Shin Bet investigation Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has said that an entire community should not be tarnished for exercising its right to vote. The fact is that Israeli Arabs came out in record numbers to vote. That can be attributed to their anger with Netanyahu over the manner in which he conducted the campaign in Gaza after the horrific terrorist attack by Hamas on October 7, 2023. It is not only the Israeli Arabs but other sections of Jewish opinion which while outraged by Hamas terrorism were deeply disturbed by the disproportion of the Netanyahu led government’s response. They too may have swelled up the Israeli Arab parties’ numbers. Some analysts are viewing the Likud charge of foreign funding and interference in the election as a Netanyahu tactic to ensure that the Eisenkot led coalition does not even think of joining hands with the Israeli Arabs to seek to oust Netanyahu from power. In any event the prospect of the Jewish parties joining hands in a government with the Arab parties is remote. This is despite the fact that Israeli Arabs form around 20% of the country’s population. This is also because even though Israel projects itself as a democratic state which treats all its citizens equally it is in essence a Jewish state which is committed to protect the Jews especially in a land which the Jews believe was given to them by God. Israel’s Jewishness was consolidated by a ‘Basic Law’ enacted in 2018. That law proclaimed: “The land of Israel is the historical homeland of the Jewish people, in which the State of Israel was established. It also proclaimed that “The state’s language is Hebrew”. The only concession it made to Arab Israelis was “The Arabic language has a special status in the state; Regulating the use of Arabic in state institutions or by them will be set in law”. With 19 seats the Arab parties are now in a position to disrupt Israel’s political process. That is intolerable for most Jews. A number of options are under consideration of how the results of this election can be preserved. Under Israeli laws the President will be obliged to go through the motions of asking some leaders to form a coalition government. One can only be formed if some parties in Eisenkot’s coalition go to Netanyahu. That seems difficult to foresee but not as difficult as Eisenkot attracting the ultra-right-wing parties from Netanyahu’s coalition. Most likely Israel will head to another election. Meanwhile, Netanyahu will continue as a care-taker Prime Minister.

stories.headline: Election Commission’s appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions
stories.title: Election Commission’s appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions
stories.summary: The officials who filed appeals against the inclusion of the 16.10 lakh voters may not have had the authority to do so under the Representation of the People Act; according to the Act, the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are the authorities with respect to electoral rolls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A little over 16 lakh electors in West Bengal whose names had been cleared by judicial officers after being flagged for logical discrepancies during the West Bengal SIR had found themselves back in the crosshairs when the Election Commission of India (ECI) filed appeals against the inclusion of their names.
These electors would have voted in the Assembly polls in April because their names appeared on the supplementary lists published before the elections.
But the officials who filed appeals against the inclusion of the 16.10 lakh voters may not have had the authority to do so under the Representation of the People Act.
According to the Act, the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are the authorities with respect to electoral rolls.

In its affidavit filed before the Supreme Court on October 26, the Election Commission of India said that the appeals were not brought to its notice earlier and that a communication dated October 22, 2026, was received from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal, stating that its officials had filed the appeals in their capacity as authorities under the Act.
It further said that the “officers had the authority to file the appeals as per the orders of this Hon’ble (Supreme) Court”.

Though the ECI, in the affidavit, mentioned that the only authorities vis-à-vis electoral rolls recognised under the Act are the “CEO/DEOs/EROs/AEROs”, it did not state categorically that the appeals against inclusions were filed by these authorised officials, and mentioned them as “officers of the office of CEO West Bengal”.
The filing of appeals against voters cleared by judicial officers was one of the questions raised by Election Commissioners S. S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi in their file notings.
Opposition parties in West Bengal have called for the scrapping of these appeals and sought a judicial probe into the matter.

According to Congress leader Prasenjit Bose, one of the petitioners in the West Bengal SIR case in the top court, these “officers of the office of the CEO” who have filed appeals against inclusion in the Appellate Tribunals cannot have any authority under the Act since the Tribunals were created by the Supreme Court in April 2026 and the Act says nothing about any tribunal.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Congress, in a memorandum submitted to the CEO of West Bengal, demanded that the appeals against inclusion filed by the ECI be cancelled, as they violated the Act.
It demanded an IT audit to disclose the date, time and process of filing these appeals.

stories.headline: Bajaj, TVS, Hero post strong Q2 profit; industry sales grow 27 percent
stories.title: Bajaj, TVS, Hero post strong Q2 profit; industry sales grow 27 percent
stories.summary: The top three listed two-wheeler makers reported strong revenue growth in the September quarter as domestic demand, an export surge and fast-rising e-scooter sales outweighed a sharp rise in commodity costs. Margins and profit growth varied across the players.Bajaj Auto, the first among the three to report its results, posted its first-ever Rs 20,000 crore revenue quarter.Revenue from operations rose 34 percent to Rs 20,003 crore, and net profit rose 35 percent to Rs 3,354 crore. Ebitda climbed 37 percent to Rs 4,172 crore. The margin was 20.9 percent, up 40 basis points from a year earlier and flat from the June quarter. Total volumes rose 20 percent to 15.49 lakh units, led by exports.TVS Motor reported revenue of Rs 17,103 crore, up 44 percent, with Ebitda up 47 percent at Rs 2,219 crore. Its margin widened 30 basis points to 13.0 percent. Net profit rose 52 percent to Rs 1,377 crore. Sales reached a record 19.19 lakh units, up 27 percent.The country’s largest two-wheeler maker Hero MotoCorp had the weakest earnings growth of the three.Standalone revenue rose 21 percent to Rs 14,687 crore and Ebitda rose 8 percent to Rs 1,968 crore. Net profit grew 5 percent to Rs 1,456 crore. Its Ebitda margin was 13.4 percent, up 10 basis points from the June quarter but down about 164 bps YoY.On a consolidated basis, Hero’s profit rose 41 percent to Rs 1,861 crore, helped by a one-time Rs 397 crore gain from the equity dilution of an associate company after its capital raise.Even in terms of sales volumes, Hero had the weakest rise, with wholesale volumes up 10.5 percent to 18.68 lakh units.Explaining the reasons behind Hero’s Q2 performance, Jay Kale, Director-Institutional Equity Research at Elara Capital, said: "Hero’s EV business is just ramping up, so commodity pressures in terms of EV losses are higher for them compared to the others. For Bajaj and TVS, a better exports mix and favourable currency movement helped offset the rise in commodity costs.”Also Read: Bajaj Auto Q2 profit jumps 35 percent to Rs 3,353 crore as exports surgeIndustry DemandHero said industry retail sales rose more than 27 percent in the quarter, with internal combustion engine (ICE) models up 23 percent and electric vehicles up 82 percent.For the first half, retail rose over 20 percent, said Hero MotoCorp CEO Harshavardhan Chitale on a post-earnings call with analysts.“To understand the impact of pent-up demand of GST, we looked at growth over the two-year period [so as to strip out the impact], which was 11 percent CAGR. This shows that industry as a whole has a healthy growth momentum, even after discounting the impact of the pent-up demand,” he said.Bajaj said the industry, including electric scooters, grew 18 percent in April-August. On a post-earnings call, the management singled out motorcycles of 150cc and above and electric scooters as the main drivers.The GST cut that took effect on September 22, 2025, lowered the tax on smaller two-wheelers, and will make YoY comparisons harder in the second half.OutlookManagement at all three expect growth to slow from the pace witnessed in H1.Hero’s Chitale said he expects the industry to grow at mid-to-high single digits in the festive period and the second half. ICE models should grow at low single digits, with EVs lifting the overall number.TVS Managing Director K N Radhakrishnan, on an analyst call, said he expects “good single-digit” growth in the third quarter, citing a high base from last year.Bajaj Joint Managing Director Rakesh Sharma expects September-December growth to stay in double digits but below the April-August rate.Also Read: Ather Energy posts first profit as EV demand outstrips supplyRural DemandThe monsoon this year is the weakest in over a decade, with a 13 percent deficit in rainfall. Parts of India are also facing droughts.Hero said rural performance matched or beat urban in the quarter and so far in the festive period. Fears of a weak monsoon have not fully played out, with sowing close to last year’s level, it said.TVS said EV growth in rural markets was slightly higher than in urban markets in the first half.Bajaj was more cautious. Sharma said that drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, parts of the south and the northeast could hurt more in the fourth quarter. He said growth is skewed toward higher-income buyers, with entry-level products lagging, a “K-shaped” pattern that may get sharper.Input CostsBajaj said commodity and other input inflation was about 3-3.5 percent of revenue in the quarter, on top of about 4.5 percent in the first.The magnitude of this cost escalation is ‘unprecedented’, creating significant pressure on the business with inflation of a scale that we would typically see spread over many years, the management said.Price increases covered 50-60 percent of the impact in the first half. The balance was largely offset through favourable currency realisation and continued cost optimisation initiatives, it said.TVS said material costs rose about 1.9 percent from the June quarter, against price hikes of 1.6 percent. article_sentences: The Election Commission of India (EC) told the Supreme Court on Friday (October 30, 2026) that though it found “false” Form 7s for deletion of voters during the Uttar Pradesh Special Intensive Revision (SIR), none of them were accepted.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the ECI, said corrective measures were taken promptly on discovery of such “false” forms.
Authorities had rejected Form 7s filed in violation of norms, the ECI said.

The ECI was responding to allegations levelled in a petition filed by Congress’ Barabanki MP Tanuj Punia, represented by senior advocate Salman Khurshid and advocate Shariq Ahmed, about widespread misuse and fraud in connection with bulk filing of Form 7 during the claims-and-objections phase of the Uttar Pradesh SIR.
Mr. Ahmed questioned the ECI’s claim that false Form 7s were stopped at the gates.
He said the court must subject this claim to judicial scrutiny.
Counsel argued that it was exactly the lack of any corrective measures in the Uttar Pradesh SIR that “emboldened” the filing of bulk Form 7s in Karnataka and Telangana.
“Of the 32 Form 7s in the Hata Assembly constituency in Uttar Pradesh, two were signed by the booth-level officer.
All these forms pertained to deletion of voters belonging to one community,” counsel submitted.
The court asked Mr. Ahmed to submit a note with details and additional information, if any, on the issue.
“Let the ECI look into these issues, take necessary action and file a compliance report,” the court observed.
The Uttar Pradesh SIR process ended in April with the final voter list showing a reported 84 lakh increase in the electorate to 13.39 crore.

stories.headline: Rising power bills spark resentment across Kashmir
stories.title: Rising power bills spark resentment across Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 29: Consumers across several parts of Kashmir have expressed resentment over the recent electricity tariff hike, alleging that rising bills and irregular power supply have added to the financial burden on ordinary households. After an elected government returned to power in Jammu and Kashmir, many residents had hoped for relief from rising living costs. However, consumers say the reported six percent increase in electricity tariffs, along with alleged hikes exceeding nine percent in some non-metered areas, has left them disappointed. Consumers have questioned the gap between the government's promises of relief, including the proposed benefit of 200 units of free electricity for eligible households, and the bills they claim to be receiving. Advocate G. N. Bukhari, who practices at the Additional District & Sessions Court, Handwara, raised concerns over electricity bills issued to consumers in North Kashmir. He alleged that some households had received bills showing increases beyond the approved six percent hike, with certain consumers claiming that their bills had nearly doubled. "Consumers from North Kashmir have every right to know why their electricity bills are increasing beyond the announced tariff revision. The authorities must explain the basis of these charges and ensure that no household is overbilled," Bukhari said. Local residents said the situation was particularly difficult for families dependent on daily wages, who are already struggling to manage household expenses amid rising prices. Shamim Ahmad, a resident of Langate and a daily-wage laborer of the Jal Shakti Department, said his electricity bill had increased from Rs 1,300 in the previous month to Rs 1,420 for September. "I earn my livelihood through daily labor. Some days I find work, while on other days I return home empty-handed. My electricity bill has increased despite our limited income. It becomes difficult to manage household expenses when every essential service keeps getting costlier," he said. Ahmad questioned the increase in his bill and urged the authorities to verify the charges. "People like us cannot afford unexpected increases in monthly bills. If the approved hike is six percent, the authorities should explain why consumers are being charged more," he added. Residents have demanded transparency in tariff calculations and sought an explanation from the Kashmir Power Distribution Corporation Limited (KPDCL) regarding the complaints. They urged the government and the Power Development Department to investigate allegations of inflated billing, verify meter readings, review tariff calculations, and ensure that consumers are charged strictly according to approved rates. However, none of the officials from KPDCL were available to comment on this issue.

After an elected government returned to power in Jammu and Kashmir, many residents had hoped for relief from rising living costs.
body: However, consumers say the reported six percent increase in electricity tariffs, along with alleged hikes exceeding nine percent in some non-metered areas, has left them disappointed.

Consumers have questioned the gap between the government's promises of relief, including the proposed benefit of 200 units of free electricity for eligible households, and the bills they claim to be receiving.
Advocate G. N. Bukhari, who practices at the Additional District & Sessions Court, Handwara, raised concerns over electricity bills issued to consumers in North Kashmir.
He alleged that some households had received bills showing increases beyond the approved six percent hike, with certain consumers claiming that their bills had nearly doubled.
"Consumers from North Kashmir have every right to know why their electricity bills are increasing beyond the announced tariff revision.
The authorities must explain the basis of these charges and ensure that no household is overbilled," Bukhari said.
Local residents said the situation was particularly difficult for families dependent on daily wages, who are already struggling to manage household expenses amid rising prices.
Shamim Ahmad, a resident of Langate and a daily-wage laborer of the Jal Shakti Department, said his electricity bill had increased from Rs 1,300 in the previous month to Rs 1,420 for September.
"I earn my livelihood through daily labor.
Some days I find work, while on other days I return home empty-handed.
My electricity bill has increased despite our limited income.
It becomes difficult to manage household expenses when every essential service keeps getting costlier," he said.
Ahmad questioned the increase in his bill and urged the authorities to verify the charges.
"People like us cannot afford unexpected increases in monthly bills.
If the approved hike is six percent, the authorities should explain why consumers are being charged more," he added.
Residents have demanded transparency in tariff calculations and sought an explanation from the Kashmir Power Distribution Corporation Limited (KPDCL) regarding the complaints.

They urged the government and the Power Development Department to investigate allegations of inflated billing, verify meter readings, review tariff calculations, and ensure that consumers are charged strictly according to approved rates.
However, none of the officials from KPDCL were available to comment on this issue.

stories.headline: From Indira to Modi
stories.title: From Indira to Modi
stories.summary: In a tight-spot after storm whipped up by the newly born Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on the shear strength of Gen Z raking up NEET and other examination paper leaks, and related fallacies in the education system affecting the youth; although the issue was already being raised by Congress leader Mr Rahul Gandhi but got a fillip after the Gen Z movement. The Narendra Modi government and the ruling BJP-led alliance (though some of the ruling allies have exhibited their unease over the issue), has endeavoured to see red in the expression ‘regime change’. It seems to be an attempt to corner the opposition I.N.D.I.A bloc and the CJP, they have only talked about peaceful protest as means of change, through the narrative of ‘regime change’ and portray them as “working against the national interest”. The ruling dispensation of the current era (read BJP) have perfected the art of setting narratives and counter-narratives as diversionary tactics and as means to corner the political opponents. In the process, not minding even if the process becomes vicious. This process in itself seems to have reached a saturation stage and with entire gamut of SIR-related operation of the ECI getting public traction, they need to relook into this strategy with a positive frame of mind. Yes, Mr Gandhi, other leaders of the opposition alliance, CJP/other youth leaders and social activist/lawyer Mr Prashant Bhushan, have been facing a major political backlash from the BJP and indirectly from the government over remarks regarding “regime change”. The ire is directed more against them for targeting the Narendra Modi government under the garb of happenings in the ECI. Why has the word regime and phrase “regime change” suddenly become a hot potato for BJP to handle? Or does this reflect signs of insecurity for the “most powerful” government/ruling party in the world? What is the dictionary meaning of the word regime? It is just for the sake of clarity on something which is nothing new to be used in political parlance of the country and which found a greater expression in the then opposition leaders, including towering one of the then Bharatiya Jan Sangh (BJS) and now BJP, scathing attacks against Prime Minister Mrs Indira Gandhi particularly on imposition of internal emergency in 1975. The powerful opposition brigade using the term “Indira regime” (reference to the authoritarian nature of her administration) and the far-cry to oust it was led by Congress (O) leader and later Prime Minister Mr Morarji Desai. It included top BJS leader Mr Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Mr L K Advani, apart from Mr Jayaprakash Narayan who spearheaded campaign against Mrs Gandhi, another former Prime Minister Ch Charan Singh and socialist leader Mr Geroge Fernandes. And many others and including the maverick Mr Raj Narain who defeated Mrs Gandhi in Rai Barelli. According to AI a regime is a system or method of governing a country, organization, or institution, or the specific group of people currently holding power. The Cambridge dictionary terms it as a particular government or system or method of government. The Wikipedia defines it; in the context of national politics, it typically refers to the system of political organization that determines access to public office, and the extent of power held by officials. Does in any way, under the shadow of these definitions and given the history of Indira Gandhi-era, expression “regime change” reflect hatching of a conspiracy? It does not seem so. And on top of that a strong dispensation such as Narendra Modi government need not fear what at best could be the political usage of the expression. They have the wherewithal to expose conspiracy, if any. Political scientists often categorize regimes as being democratic, autocratic, or hybrid in the academic sense of the term. However, in everyday language, a regime is an authoritarian or unjust government. There is nothing unparliamentary or unconstitutional in these expressions which were very rightly used, at times even crossing limits of niceties, during the 1975-77 phase by the then opposition leaders and their young cadres. In the present context the ‘regime change’ mention has come in the light of alleged charges of manipulating electoral rolls with a motive to help the ruling party. Obviously, the reference has been made in order to build public opinion and convince the people that their votes could be safeguarded only through a ‘regime change’. The underlining factor is voter-lists without wholesale deletions and alleged arbitrary inclusions, and which are above any doubt. The BJP strategists seem to have lapped up the ‘regime change’ opportunity with both the hands. The party president, Mr Nitin Nabin led the charge through a post on ‘X’ which read; “The use of terms like ‘regime change’ has exposed the true agenda of the opposition….. This nefarious attempt to destabilise India in collusion with foreign powers is part of the agenda of ‘urban naxals’. The opposition’s fight is not for electoral reforms, SIR, or the future of the country’s youth… but rather to spread anarchy in the country and seize power at any cost.” Mr Nabin must decipher from the archives, as he was born in the year when the party which he heads now was born in 1980, as to how often phrase ‘regime change’ was used by his senior leaders and how often Mrs Gandhi and her coterie described the opposition’s movement as aided and abetted by foreign powers. Colourful theories were touted by the then opposition leaders as to how erstwhile USSR was helping Mrs Gandhi win elections through the use of a mysterious ink-pad and ballot paper; wherever you stamp it will appear on Congress symbol, was the oft repeated charge. Fact of the matter is that despite all such charges flying thick and high and the “mysterious foreign hand” at play, Mrs Gandhi lost the election in 1977, even losing her own seat. Majority of the opposition leaders including Mr Vajpayee and Mr Advani won the election to become Union Ministers for the first time. The ‘regime change’ had taken place through an impartial, free and fair election for which credit must go to Mrs Gandhi, notwithstanding excesses committed during the imposition of internal emergency. The ‘regime change’ did not connote any conspiracy at that point in time and the expression is finding place during the present movement against SIR and other failures of the government, in the same spirit. As a counter to BJP president’s assertion invoking “urban naxal and foreign powers” syndrome behind opposition’s ‘regime change’ metaphor, opposition is firm on its stand and so are the CJP activists. Mr Gandhi and other opposition alliance leaders maintain that their protests and criticisms are rooted in constitutional rights, democratic resistance, and fighting alleged capture of state institutions. And that there is nothing unconstitutional, illegal or anti-national in talking of a “regime change” using peaceful means through the expression of ballot.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to take measures against online misuse of court feeds
stories.summary: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submits that suggestions from various High Courts and other stakeholders have been received and forwarded to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 30, 2026) asked the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to formulate measures against the commercial exploitation of live-streamed judicial proceedings in violation of earlier court orders.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant recorded Solicitor General Tushar Mehta’s submission that suggestions from various High Courts and other stakeholders had already been received and forwarded to the Ministry.
Mr. Mehta submitted that the Ministry would consider the suggestions and respond in a few days.
He sought listing of the plea for further consideration after the Deepavali vacation.
He also flagged violations of earlier orders and urged the court to consider directing the removal of material uploaded in breach of its restrictions.

The court had recently passed orders banning the unauthorised use and circulation of live-streamed judicial proceedings on social media and digital platforms, saying that anything meant for the public good cannot be exploited commercially for personal gain.
“Necessary measures for taking action against those who fail to comply with the directions will also be incorporated in the policy regime,” the court observed.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan suggested that every official clip released by the court should carry a verifiable digital signature or watermark, enabling the public and digital platforms to distinguish genuine footage from manipulated versions.
He further suggested that all court proceedings should be made available on the Supreme Court’s website in an authenticated and watermarked format.

The court is examining the issue amid concerns over the unauthorised extraction, modification, circulation, and commercial use of video clips of judicial proceedings, often accompanied by misleading captions or representations.
